title: Implement error budget computation job/service + storage model for dashboards and release gates
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
We need a canonical error budget computation component that continuously computes budget remaining + burn rates for tiered SLOs (Hosted + Dedicated) and powers: (1) SLO/budget dashboards in Console/Grafana, (2) burn-rate alerts, and (3) CI/CD + rollout gates via a budget-check API.

This ticket covers the computation job/service (scheduled workflow is acceptable for v1), a minimal data model, and a storage plan that supports: latest budget snapshot lookups (low-latency) + short retention history for charts/forecast overlays.

Context:
- SLO definitions live in Confluence and will be encoded via slo-toolkit tier-aware schema.
- We need consistent semantics across teams so the same numbers show up in dashboards, alerts, and deploy gates.

Links:
- Confluence: Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/tiered-slo-definitions-hosted-vs-dedicated.json
- Confluence: Error budget policy + enforcement: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/error-budget-policy-and-enforcement.json
- GitHub (reference libs): sources/github/slo-toolkit/pull_request_118.json, sources/github/slo-toolkit/pull_request_121.json
- Related: ENG-2422 (gate integration), ENG-2425 (dashboards), ENG-2420 (burn alerts)

Owner notes:
- Aisha to own implementation + integration with Logan/Nadia for data correctness.
- Benji/Ethan are consumers via control plane budget-check endpoint + pipeline step; we should align early on query shape + caching semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Given a tier-aware SLO config (Hosted/Dedicated), the system computes: budget_remaining (0..1), budget_burn_rate (per window), and burn alerts can be derived from the same underlying numbers.
Latest budget status can be fetched for a scope (tier, service, region, route, model, customer_pool where applicable) in <250ms p95 from the budget-check API consumer perspective (can be cached).
Budget computation supports rolling windows at minimum: 30d (primary), plus 1h/6h/24h burn-rate helper windows needed for multi-window alerting.
Writes are bounded by cardinality budget guidance (no unbounded per-request IDs; avoid per-customer metrics in Hosted; Dedicated customer pool IDs only where explicitly required).
Dashboards can plot budget remaining over time for at least 14 days without expensive Prometheus range queries (store computed history).
Backfill path exists (even if manual) to validate targets and calibrate alert thresholds (ties to ENG-2429).
Runbook references and owner annotations are included in stored records or emitted metrics labels so alert payloads can include links.
proposed_design:
Summary
We will implement a small internal service ("budgetd") that runs on a fixed schedule (every 60s) to compute error budget remaining + burn rates for each published SLO objective.

Inputs
1) SLO config (tier-aware) from slo-toolkit (checked into repo and deployed with service). v1 expects config changes via PR (not UI).
2) SLI time series from Prometheus via remote-read (preferred) or pre-aggregated metrics exported by gateway/routing/runtime.

Computation model
- For each SLO objective O, define:
  - objective.target (e.g., 99.9% success)
  - objective.window (e.g., 30d rolling)
  - objective.sli_query (success / total, or error / total)
  - objective.dimensions (tier/region/route/model; Dedicated may include pool_id)
- Compute:
  - error_budget_total = 1 - target
  - error_budget_used = max(0, observed_bad_rate - 0) (observed_bad_rate is derived from SLI over the rolling window)
  - budget_remaining = clamp(1 - (observed_bad_rate / error_budget_total), 0, 1)
  - burn_rate(window_x) = observed_bad_rate(window_x) / error_budget_total

Note: We will store both observed_good_rate and observed_bad_rate explicitly to reduce ambiguity.

Storage plan
We need two types of storage:
A) Latest snapshot key-value for gates + fast lookups.
B) Short retention time series for dashboards/overlays.

Plan (v1)
- Postgres (control plane shared cluster) for latest snapshots + metadata:
  - slo_objectives (id, name, tier, service, route, model, region, pool_id?, target, window_seconds, owner_team, runbook_url, created_at, updated_at)
  - budget_snapshots_latest (objective_id, as_of_ts, good_events, bad_events, total_events, observed_bad_rate, budget_remaining, burn_rate_1h, burn_rate_6h, burn_rate_24h, computation_version)
  - budget_overrides (objective_id, override_state, reason, created_by, approved_by, expires_at, created_at) [used by gates; write path may come later but schema reserved]
- ClickHouse for timeseries history (14d retention to start):
  - budget_snapshots_history (objective_id, as_of_ts, budget_remaining, burn_rate_1h, burn_rate_6h, burn_rate_24h, observed_bad_rate, total_events)

Why ClickHouse?
- We already use it for high-cardinality observability slices; it is cheaper than long Prometheus range queries for rendering dashboards across many dimensions.
- It supports fast time-bucket queries for charting budget remaining and correlating with deploy events.

Metrics output
- budgetd also emits Prometheus gauges so alerting can stay in Prometheus:
  - redwood_budget_remaining{objective_id,tier,service,region,route,model,pool_id?}
  - redwood_burn_rate{objective_id,window="1h|6h|24h"...}
- We will keep label sets aligned with the cardinality proposal (ENG-2424). objective_id will be the stable join key for dashboards.

API surface (for gates/dashboards)
- Internal gRPC/HTTP endpoint (consumed by control plane budget-check endpoint in redwood):
  - GET /v1/budgets/latest?scope=... returns status for matching objectives
  - Response includes: objective metadata + budget_remaining + burn rates + as_of_ts + override_state
- v1 will support only "latest" reads; history reads can be served via ClickHouse queries in dashboards backend (or later via a dedicated budgets API).

Deployment
- budgetd runs in platform cluster, one active instance per environment (prod/staging), with leader election.
- Schedule: every 60s compute; each run bounded by objective count and query cost.

Guardrails
- Hard cap the number of objective series computed per run (config validation) to avoid runaway due to accidental dimension explosion.
- Validate queries at startup and expose a "computation health" endpoint with last successful run timestamp + per-objective errors.

Open question
- If ClickHouse is not acceptable for v1, fallback is Postgres-only (store 14d of snapshots at 1m granularity = ~20k rows per objective per 14d; likely too large for high objective counts). ClickHouse strongly preferred.
implementation_plan: Finalize storage choice w/ Logan Wright (Telemetry) and get tables approved (Postgres + ClickHouse).
Define objective_id strategy (hash of normalized objective key fields + config version) to keep stable joins and avoid collisions.
Implement budgetd core loop (scheduler + per-objective compute) using slo-toolkit library helpers (PR #118).
Implement Prometheus remote-read client + query templates; add per-query timeout + retry with circuit-breaker to avoid dogpiling Prometheus under incident load.
Write latest snapshots to Postgres (transactional upsert) and history snapshots to ClickHouse (batched inserts).
Emit Prometheus gauges from budgetd (optional in v1, but needed for ENG-2420 alerting standardization).
Add integration contract tests: known synthetic time series -> expected budget_remaining + burn_rate calculations (esp around low volume + division-by-zero).
Stage rollout in staging with 5-10 objectives (Hosted chat streaming + embeddings + Dedicated readiness), verify against manual query results in SLI validation scratchpad.
Prod rollout behind feature flag; start with warn-only gate consumers (ENG-2422).
Add oncall/runbook entry: budgetd failure modes (Prometheus query failures, ClickHouse insert lag, Postgres contention) and what dashboards/gates do when data stale.
risks_and_mitigations:
1) Cardinality explosion
Risk: objective dimensions (tier/region/route/model) multiplied by per-model and per-route breakdown can create thousands of objectives.
Mitigation: enforce config validation caps + require explicit allowlists for model/route splits; align with ENG-2424.

2) Data correctness / attribution
Risk: mismatch between logs vs metrics, or misclassification of streaming disconnects/timeouts causing false budget burn and bad gate outcomes.
Mitigation: partner with Nadia Rahman to validate against log-based counts; implement per-objective "data_quality" tag and do not hard-block gates when data_quality=degraded (warn-only) until validated.

3) Staleness
Risk: budgetd fails or Prometheus is degraded during incidents, making gates block or dashboards misleading.
Mitigation: include as_of_ts and staleness thresholds; gates should treat stale data as "unknown" and follow policy (initially warn-only). Emit 'budgetd_last_success_ts' metric.

4) Performance / load on Prometheus
Risk: budgetd remote-read queries can overload Prometheus during widespread incidents.
Mitigation: query batching, strict timeouts, and backoff; keep computation frequency configurable; consider pre-aggregated recording rules for heavy objectives.
open_questions: Do we want the "source of truth" to be computed from Prometheus metrics only, or can we compute from ClickHouse logs for certain SLIs (e.g., streaming disconnect taxonomy)?
How do we represent Dedicated customer pools: pool_id only, or (customer_id, pool_id)? Proposal: pool_id only to avoid customer PII and reduce join complexity.
Do we need separate budgets for TTFT vs end-to-end streaming duration latency SLIs, or only availability/disconnect initially? (Thread ongoing in ENG-2428).
Retention requirement for budget history: 14d vs 30d. Proposal: 14d now; add downsampled 30d later.
